name: capture
summary: a windows desktop experiment for user-triggered region capture and AI-assisted editor input. separates the background app from a status monitor, with pause, cancellation, and offline rehearsal controls. screenshots are submitted only on an explicit action.
problem: Explore a user-controlled workflow for selecting a screen region, requesting AI assistance, and replaying generated text into an editor, with explicit pause and cancellation controls.
highlights: Explicit submission: Select a region first, then submit it through a separate action. Capturing a region does not itself send an API request.
Separate status monitor: The background application owns capture and input handling; a separate monitor reports state without taking over its lifecycle.
Rehearsal & cancellation: An offline rehearsal mode exercises the workflow with a fixed snippet. Pause, restart, and cancellation controls manage local state.

media.caption: Actual offline core-module output: selection normalization, character stepping, and rejecting a stale response after reset. Styled terminal presentation; no API calls or input hooks.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Start the app and enable the controls.
- Select the intended region and explicitly submit it.
- Review request state in the monitor.
- Replay, pause, or discard generated editor input.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: Python coordinates Windows input hooks, screen capture, API requests, process ownership, and a separate monitoring process. Local rehearsal avoids live API traffic during workflow checks.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: A Windows-specific experiment. Editor focus, keyboard layouts, and automatic indentation affect replay. Local cancellation discards the answer but cannot undo a request already received by the provider.
